cohort: The study included 728 pregnant women delivering after 37 weeks at one University hospital/tertiary care referral center, with 662 women analyzed for a complete Nugent Score of the vaginal swab.
finding: There was no significant association between the presence of bacterial vaginosis and the incidence of perineal tears during vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Instrumental delivery was identified as the most important risk factor for perineal lacerations.
